Right now you're starting from a blank slate — no Code Connect files, no Figma config in the repo, and no saved memory. That's exactly why you have to point me to the design system every time. Here's the honest picture of what's possible and how to fix it.

## Short answer: yes, and there are three layers to it

**1. Save the "where" once → I recall it every session (cheapest, do this first)**

The reason you re-point me each time is that nothing persists between sessions. I can write a memory file recording your design system's coordinates:
- Figma **file key** (the `xxxx` in `figma.com/design/xxxx/...`)
- The library/team name and the node IDs of your main component & variable pages

Once that's saved, every new session I already know "the design system lives *here*" without you saying a word. This is the single highest-leverage step and takes 30 seconds.

**2. Code Connect files → automatic component↔code mapping (the real automation)**

This is the mechanism the Figma MCP is actually built around. You create `*.figma.ts` files that map each Figma component to its React/code counterpart (props, variants, the works). Once they exist in your repo:
- I (and the `figma-generate-design` / `figma-code-connect` skills) **auto-discover** them — no pointing needed.
- "Build the game-over modal using our design system" → I pull the right components, variants, and tokens automatically because the mapping is on disk.

This is the difference between "find something that looks right" and "use *our* button, with *our* variants."

**3. A short design-system block in CLAUDE.md → always-loaded rules**

Things like "always use tokens, never hardcode hex" or "primary components live in library X" go in CLAUDE.md so they're loaded into context on every task automatically.

## The tradeoff

| Layer | Effort | Payoff |
|---|---|---|
| Memory pointer | ~1 min | I stop asking "where's your design system" |
| CLAUDE.md rules | ~5 min | Consistent token/component conventions |
| Code Connect | ~real work (per component) | True automation — I assemble from *your* system |

Code Connect is where the magic is, but it's an investment — one file per component you want mapped. The other two are nearly free and remove 80% of the friction immediately.

## What I'd suggest

Let me set up layers 1 and 2 now. To do that I need one thing from you: **the Figma file URL (or file key) of your design system / component library.** Paste it and I'll:
1. Inspect it via the Figma MCP to catalog your components, variables, and styles
2. Write a memory file + a CLAUDE.md design-system section so it's never re-explained
3. Show you what a Code Connect file would look like for one component, so you can decide whether to roll it out further

Want me to go ahead? Just drop the Figma link.

content.text:
Yes — but it's a different setup, and one piece of the magic doesn't carry over. Let me be precise about what does and doesn't.

## What's the same vs. different

Claude Desktop and Claude Code are two different runtimes. The Figma *MCP tools* can run in both, but the **persistence layers** I described work differently:

| Layer | Claude Code (here) | Claude Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| Figma MCP tools | ✅ already connected | ✅ via `claude_desktop_config.json` |
| "Remember where my design system is" | memory files + CLAUDE.md | ✅ **Projects** → custom instructions + knowledge files |
| Auto-rules ("always use tokens") | CLAUDE.md | ✅ Project custom instructions |
| **Code Connect auto-discovery** | ✅ reads `*.figma.ts` from your repo | ⚠️ **weak** — no repo access by default |
| Figma skills (`figma-generate-design`, etc.) | ✅ | ❌ not available in Desktop |

## The honest catch

The two cheap layers transfer cleanly. In Claude Desktop you'd use a **Project** instead of CLAUDE.md/memory: set the custom instructions to name your design system + tokens-not-hex rules, and the Project carries that into every chat automatically. Same effect — no re-pointing.

But the deepest layer — **Code Connect** — is where Desktop falls short:
- Those `.figma.ts` mappings live in your **codebase**. Claude Code reads your filesystem natively; Claude Desktop doesn't, unless you also add a **Filesystem MCP server** pointed at the repo.
- And even with filesystem access, Desktop doesn't run the `figma-generate-design`/`figma-code-connect` **skills** that orchestrate the "assemble a page from our components" workflow. You'd be doing it with raw MCP tool calls and a lot more manual steering.

## Practical recommendation

- **For "I want to chat with Figma and have it know my design system"** → Claude Desktop + a Project works great. Cheap and persistent.
- **For "build/update real screens from our actual coded components"** → Claude Code is the stronger tool, because the design-system↔code integration (Code Connect + skills + repo access) only fully exists here.

A common split people use: do the code-side work (Code Connect, building screens) in Claude Code, and use Claude Desktop Projects for lightweight design conversations and ideation.

### Two setup steps for Desktop, if you want them
1. **Connect the Figma MCP**: add the Figma server block to `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, then restart the app.
2. **Create a Project** named e.g. "Chess UI Design System," and in its custom instructions paste the design-system summary (file key, library, token rules).

I can generate both for you — the exact `claude_desktop_config.json` block and the Project instructions text — once you give me that Figma file link. Want me to?
